messages.author: 6a288128bce8283d
messages.subject: Multi-species data
parts:
Hello again!

As I would like to try some multi-species model runs I was wondering,
if that is in general possible with the unmarked functions (I wasn't
able to find anything on that)?

And secondly:
which format would my data have to be in to work with this?
I know from PRESENCE of the following 2 options:

Option 1. Create presence/absence data for species A as you would for
a single-species analysis. Create presence/absence data for species B.
Tack species B data in rows after species A data. So, if you have 100
sites, the first 100 rows of data will be presence/absence for species
A, and the 2nd 100 rows will be the data for species B. Duplicate
covariate data to match corresponding rows in presence/absence data.

Option 2. Create presence/absence data where '1' =species A only
detected, '2' = species B only detected, '3'=both species detected,
and '0'=neither species detected. So, if you have 100 sites, you'll
have 100 rows and no duplication of covariates is necessary.

Are they applicable here too?

Thank you for your help,
Richard

messages.author: 9548b9e0c8258268
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Multi-species data
parts:
Hi Richard,

Unmarked does not currently fit any multi-species models, but this
would be an excellent future feature
(http://github.com/ianfiske/unmarked/issues#issue/28).

Best,
Ian

messages.author: 2bd0159ce8ff57b4
messages.subject: Error in modSel when specifying null model
parts:
Greetings,

I have the most up to date version of unmarked (v unmarked_0.8-5), but I am running into a strange error when I attempt model selection while specifying a null model. I have tried it a couple of ways (see reproducible code below). Any suggestions would be welcome. Thank you.

The error reads as follows:
Error in .local(object, ...) :
nullmod must be character name of null model fit in the fitlist.

Code:

library(unmarked)#Load unmarked
data(frogs)#Data frame
M <- nrow(pfer.bin)
J <- ncol(pfer.bin)
SiteCovs <- siteCovs <- data.frame(sitevar1 = rnorm(M))
ObsCovs <- obsCovs <- data.frame(obsvar1 = rnorm(M*J))
siteCovs$sitevar1 <- scale(siteCovs$sitevar1)
obsCovs$obsvar1 <- scale(obsCovs$obsvar1)
pferUMF1 <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y=pfer.bin,siteCovs = siteCovs,obsCovs = obsCovs)

#Run three models
fm.1 <- occu(~ obsvar1 ~ 1, pferUMF1)
fm.2 <- occu(~ 1 ~ 1, pferUMF1)#Null model
fm.3 <- occu(~obsvar1 ~ sitevar1, pferUMF1)

#Fit list of models
models <- fitList(fm.1,fm.2,fm.3)

#Run model selection specifyin fm.2 as a null model
modSel(models, nullmod = fm.2)

#Try again but specifyin fm.2 as a character
modSel(models, nullmod = "fm.2")

messages.author: eb5eaa0c2c4552cd
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error in modSel when specifying null model
parts:
Looks like the old bug was fixed and a new one was added. The way it
is now, you need to name the models. For example, this works:

models <- fitList(m1 = fm.1, m2 = fm.2, m3 = fm.3)
modSel(models, nullmod = "m2")

We'll fix this so that you don't have to name them in fitList.

Richard
